sec: Management of Hyponatremia · acute versus chronic correction

items.q: Fill up: The management table splits at 48 hours, labelling the acute column as ______ and the chronic-onset column as ______.
items.exp: The headings are '< 48 Hours (Acute, symptomatic)' and '>48 Hours/Chronic Onset (Compensated)'. (Book p964)

items.q: Fill up: The acute column warns that a raised ______ carries a risk of ______, and that risk is stated to exceed the risk of osmotic demyelination from rapid correction.
items.exp: The listed sequence is raised ICT (intracranial tension) leading to a risk of herniation, and herniation is ranked above osmotic demyelination on rapid correction. (Book p964)

items.q: How is 3% saline prescribed in the acute symptomatic column of the management table?
opts: 3 bottles of 100 ml, each over 10 minutes, total 30 minutes
items.exp: Rx in the acute column is 3% saline as 3 bottles of 100 ml, each given over 10 minutes for a total of 30 minutes. (Book p964)

items.q: A patient with an acute symptomatic hyponatremia has completed the three 100 ml bottles of 3% saline within half an hour. Which feature on this page authorises repeating that regimen?
opts: Onset still under 48 hours or a fresh seizure
Failure of fluid restriction after 24 hours
items.exp: The acute column adds a single instruction: repeat if still under 48 hours, or if there is a fresh seizure. (Book p964)

items.q: Assess the acute column: I Rapid correction is accepted because herniation is judged the greater hazard. II The same column prescribes 3% saline as a continuous infusion at 15-30 ml/hr.
items.exp: Statement I is the page's own justification, but the acute regimen is three 100 ml bottles over 10 minutes each; the 15-30 ml/hr infusion belongs to the chronic branch with sodium under 120. (Book p964)

items.q: A 23-year-old is brought in 4 hours after a fitness challenge during which she drank about 18 L of water; sodium is 111 mEq/L and she has a generalised tonic-clonic seizure. What does this page's acute algorithm specify first?
opts: 100 ml of 3% saline over 10 minutes, repeated to three bottles
Fluid restriction to 1 L/day with observation
Tolvaptan after a baseline liver profile
Normal saline 1 L bolus then reassess
items.exp: Onset is well within 48 hours with seizures, so the acute column applies: 3% saline, 3 bottles of 100 ml, each over 10 minutes. (Book p964)

items.q: For a severe hyponatremia of chronic onset, the page offers 3% saline as 100 ml bottles in two alternative regimens. Which pair of limits does it give?
items.exp: The chronic column reads: if severe, 3 bottles of 100 ml 3% saline, 6 bottles/24 hours OR 25 ml/hr. (Book p964)

items.q: Match each branch of the chronic-onset column with its instruction — 1) Reduced IVC diameter 2) Euvolemic with sodium under 120 3) Euvolemic with sodium above 120 … A) Admit and start normal saline B) 3% saline infusion at 15-30 ml/hr C) Fluid restriction, with a vaptan as the second option
items.exp: Hypovolaemia signalled by a collapsed IVC is admitted for normal saline; euvolemic sodium below 120 gets 3% saline at 15-30 ml/hr; above 120 gets fluid restriction and vaptans. (Book p964)

items.q: A 71-year-old with chronic SIADH has sodium 127 mEq/L, clinically euvolemic and asymptomatic. What is the page's first-line measure?
items.exp: For chronic euvolemic hyponatremia above 120, the first entry is fluid restriction; vaptans are listed after it, with baseline LFT required. (Book p964)

items.q: Assess the two cautions attached to tolvaptan on this page: I Liver function tests should be checked before starting it. II It may be given freely to a dehydrated patient provided the sodium is above 120 mEq/L.
items.exp: The two caveats printed under vaptans are to check LFT before starting and not to give the drug in dehydration. (Book p964)

items.q: How is the vaptan receptor labelled on this management page, and which receptor does the ADH chapter's receptor table assign to cAMP-mediated aquaporin insertion?
opts: This page prints V_a; the receptor table assigns V2
This page prints V2; the receptor table assigns V1a
This page prints V3; the receptor table assigns V1
items.exp: The vaptan line is printed as V_a antagonists although tolvaptan and friends block the V2 receptor, the cAMP-coupled receptor listed for collecting duct AQP2 insertion. (Book p964)

items.q: Every instruction below belongs to the greater-than-48-hour column EXCEPT:
opts: Three 100 ml bottles of 3% saline, each over 10 minutes
Admit and start normal saline when the IVC diameter is reduced
3% saline infusion at 15-30 ml/hr when sodium is under 120
Fluid restriction when sodium is above 120
items.exp: The rapid three-bottle regimen over 30 minutes is the acute symptomatic arm; the other three are all branches of the compensated chronic column. (Book p964)

items.q: A 64-year-old on chlorpropamide has sodium 116 mEq/L discovered incidentally, present for an estimated 3 weeks, euvolemic with no seizures. Which regimen fits this page?
opts: 3 bottles of 100 ml each over 10 minutes
Fluid restriction and tolvaptan as the only measures
items.exp: Chronic onset with a euvolemic sodium below 120 is managed by a 3% saline infusion at 15-30 ml/hr, not by boluses and not by fluid restriction, which is reserved for values above 120. (Book p964)

items.q: In the chronic column, recognition of a reduced IVC diameter leads directly to which decision?
opts: Admit the patient and start normal saline
Start tolvaptan and restrict free water
Give three 100 ml bottles of 3% saline in 30 minutes
Recheck sodium after 24 hours of observation
items.exp: A reduced IVC diameter marks hypovolaemia, and the arrow from that box points to admitting the patient and starting normal saline. (Book p964)
